title: Perform work site insecticide, herbicide or fungicide clean-up and clearance procedures

lessons.title: Cleaning up after treatment
lessons.html:
Why clean-up matters

A treatment is not finished when the spraying stops. Left-over mix, dirty equipment, empty containers, spills and residues on surfaces can poison people, pets and livestock or pollute water long after the team has gone. Clean-up and clearance make the site safe to hand back.

Left-over product

  • Plan the mix so very little is left over.
  • Apply small remaining amounts to the target area if the label allows, without exceeding the label rate.
  • Never pour left-over mix into drains, toilets, soil, rivers or dams.
  • Return unopened concentrate to the vehicle store in its original container.

Equipment cleaning

  1. Wear PPE while cleaning.
  2. Release pressure from sprayers.
  3. Triple rinse the tank and spray the rinse water onto the treated area or into an approved rinsate collection system.
  4. Clean nozzles, filters and lances with a soft brush; never blow through nozzles by mouth.
  5. Use a tank cleaner after herbicides if the label recommends it.
  6. Wash the outside of equipment and store it secured in the vehicle.

Empty containers

Triple rinse where the label allows, puncture or crush them so they cannot be reused, and take them back for disposal through an approved route. Never leave them on site, give them to anyone, burn them or bury them.

Spills and contaminated surfaces

  • Contain spills with absorbent material, sweep it up and bag it as hazardous waste.
  • Clean contaminated hard surfaces as the SDS directs.
  • Remove any product accidentally applied to food contact surfaces and report it.
  • Collect used absorbent, rags and damaged PPE for hazardous waste disposal.

Personal decontamination

Wash gloves before taking them off, then remove PPE in the right order. Wash hands and face. Wash work clothes separately from family laundry.

lessons.title: Clearance and handing the site back
lessons.html:
What clearance means

Clearance is the decision, checked and recorded, that the treated area is safe to return to normal use. For insecticide, herbicide and fungicide treatments this depends on the label's re-entry period and any other precautions, such as ventilation or cleaning of surfaces before food handling resumes.

Clearance checks

CheckWhat to confirm
Re-entry periodThe time stated on the label has passed, or will pass before people return
VentilationIndoor areas have been aired as the label requires
SurfacesFood contact surfaces are clean and were not treated
Bait and devicesBait stations are secured, counted and recorded
WasteNo containers, rags or spilled product left on site
Outdoor areasBarriers can be removed, livestock kept out for any grazing period on the label

Handing back

  1. Walk through the area with the client contact.
  2. Remove warning notices and barriers when the re-entry period has passed, or leave them with clear instructions for the client to remove them at the stated time.
  3. Explain precautions: do not wash treated cracks for a set time, keep pets away from bait stations, or keep livestock off sprayed camps as the label requires.
  4. Give the written service report with product details, areas treated and re-entry times.
  5. Get the client's signature as required.

Records

Record clean-up, waste returned, any spill or incident and the clearance time. Reconcile product used with stock issued.

Key points

  • Never pour left-over mix or rinse water into drains, soil or water.
  • Triple rinse equipment and containers, and make containers unusable before approved disposal.
  • Contain spills and treat contaminated material as hazardous waste.
  • Clear the site only after the label re-entry period and other precautions are met.
  • Walk through with the client, explain precautions and give a written report.

quiz.question: What may you do with a small amount of left-over mix?

options.text: Apply it to the target area if the label allows, within the label rate

quiz.question: What should be done to empty containers after rinsing?

options.text: Puncture or crush them and take them for approved disposal
Leave them for the client's workers

quiz.question: Clearance after a spray treatment mainly depends on...

options.text: The label re-entry period and other precautions

quiz.question: How should gloves be handled at the end of the job?

options.text: Pulled off quickly and thrown in the cab
Washed in the client's kitchen sink

quiz.question: Where should used absorbent from a spill go?
Work clothes should be washed separately from family laundry.
Warning notices may be removed as soon as spraying ends, even if the re-entry period has not passed.
Which checks are part of clearance? (select all that apply)

options.text: No containers or rags left on site
